## Entry J-389 — M12.4 SHIPPED + CLOSED = M12 (attachments) CLOSED: erasure (redact + blob-delete + Retained-refusal); box-gated e2e green; next-active = Round-2 final pre-UI gate

**What happened.** Clair implemented M12.4 spine-first across three commits on top of the runbook `e2f7d42`; Joe pushed; the box-gated real-binary e2e RUN went green; Chat cross-verified on `main` (D-065) and landed this close bridge. **M12.4 (erasure) is SHIPPED + CLOSED — and with it the whole M12 (attachments) milestone CLOSES.** HEAD `8315f72`, tree clean, in sync with origin.

**What shipped (erasure, made real against attachments).** `message.redact` was a bare validated kind with no applier; M12.4 gives it one. On a redact, the node resolves the target `message.file`'s descriptor blob_refs and — gated on the **original content author's** `Retention` — either **deletes the blob bytes** (a real, complete erasure of that node's copy: the content-addressed `BlobStore` is mutable, separate from the DAG) or **refuses** on a Retained (T4) author (the legal-hold floor, `10004`). The redact event itself always converges; only the byte-delete side-effect is gated. The DAG-resident residue (event existence + plaintext descriptor key + text) is **not** erased — that's the D3 crypto-shred arc (WE6 boundary). The GDPR win lands on the mutable layer; the immutable residue is marked-and-reserved — the M12.3 "build the mechanism, fence the maturity" pattern.

**Commits (spine-first, per-commit DoD-gated).** runbook `e2f7d42` · **C1** `ccc267c` — `BlobStore::delete` (idempotent: `Ok(true)` removed / `Ok(false)` absent-no-op / `Err` malformed ref) + the typed `BlobError::ErasureRefusedRetained → 10004` (blob_store.rs:98; RC-F-01 re-grep confirmed 10004 free) · **C2** `16cb81f` — the spine: `build_message_redact_event` ({target_event_id}) + `NodeRuntime::resolve_redact_erasure` (a pure xgen-core decision fn at node/runtime.rs:574 — D1 target-id, V4 resolve target from the Space store, read `attachments` blob_refs, **D2/F2b read `target.sender`'s `Retention`** via `author_is_retained`, lenient: only explicit module-declared `Retained` blocks, absent/Erasable/no-module → erase per D-088 T1-max-erasable; **M12's first production `Retention` reader**) + the `process_inbound` Accepted-arm hook `apply_redact_erasure` (app.rs:3004; **D3 gate the side-effect not admission**; `RefusedRetained` → `10004` via `reject_signal` to a `LocallySubmitted` redactor; origin-agnostic → B's federated redact deletes B's cached copy = WE4) · **C3** `8315f72` — the redact CLI verb (`ops::redact` + 4-arm D-092: main.rs / app.rs / batch.rs / aicontrol.rs) + the minimal client tombstone (D6/V8: `fetch_attachments` skips a redacted `message.file`'s blob) + Appendix F v1.11→1.12 (Session 8) + the box-gated e2e (`#[ignore]`). **DoD each:** build 0-error · clippy `--all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean · in-suite `cargo test --workspace` → **1463/0** (1448 + C1's 4 + C2's 10 + C3's parse test; e2e `#[ignore]`). **RED-on-revert recorded** for the C2 spine: neuter `author_is_retained` → WE2 fails (Delete not RefusedRetained) + WE3 fails (Retained bytes deleted = legal-hold breach); restored → green.

**Box-gated e2e RUN — green (Joe ran it).** `cargo test -p xgen-mptest --test m12_4_self_thread_redact_e2e -- --ignored`: `w_redact_erases_attachment_e2e ... ok` — "redacted attachment gone, non-redacted retrievable (real binaries)," 16.97s, on the real two-same-identity-client path.

**Chat cross-verify on `main` (D-065, not by faith).** `delete` + `10004` typed (blob_store.rs:98/192); `resolve_redact_erasure` verified line-by-line (node/runtime.rs:574-623 — reads `target.sender`'s Retention, lenient, only explicit Retained blocks); the hook fires in the Accepted arm after store + before fanout (app.rs:3325, side-effect not admission); the D8 hinge verified in code — `encrypt_blob` (blob.rs:59) calls `OsRng.fill_bytes` for both key + nonce per call, the `fresh_key_and_ciphertext_each_call` test asserts `c1 != c2` → `blob_ref` per-send-unique by construction; local/remote in sync.

## Entry J-388 — M12.4 OPENED-grounded + Phase-0 audit DONE + design Joe-LOCKED: erasure (redact + blob-delete + Retained-refusal); M12.4-D1..D9; M12-D6 promoted → D-093; next-active = Clair runbook

**What happened.** Clair authored the M12.4 D-071 Phase-0 audit (audit seat) and committed it (`31e17aa`, pushed) — verdict GO, findings M12.4-A-01..09, six+ grounding facts, eight forks FK-1..FK-8 with recommendations. Chat opened the M12.4 design discussion on the eight forks + the M12-D6 promotion, recommended on each; Joe locked **all by-recomms** (two explicit Joe-locks: FK-2 the Retention-read target, and the M12-D6 promotion). Before authoring, Chat independently re-grounded the load-bearing claims on `main @ 31e17aa` (D-065) and authored `tasks/M12_4_ERASURE_DESIGN.md` (v1.0 ACTIVE) + the `DECISIONS.md` D-093 promotion + this bridge. M12.4 is the **fourth + final** M12 sub-arc; **M12.4 close = M12 close**. Doc-only; no code.

**The central enabling fact.** Attachments split content across **two stores of opposite mutability**: blob ciphertext lives in the content-addressed `BlobStore` (separate from the DAG, **mutable** → deleting bytes is a real, complete erasure of that node's copy, **buildable now**); the `message.file` event residue (existence + the plaintext per-blob key + any text) is **DAG-immutable** → crypto-shred, **D3-gated** (per M12-D10 + D-088's cascade). M12.4 builds the GDPR win on the mutable layer and marks-and-reserves the DAG residue to D3 — the M12.3 "build the mechanism, fence the maturity" pattern. This is why M12.4 is GO-able and not a repeat of Arc I's design-only close (J-253): there is a concrete mutable surface to actually erase.

**Chat re-grounding (D-065, on `main @ 31e17aa`).** `message.redact` is a bare validated kind (permission arm exchange.rs:792 → `SendMessages`, no-op validation exchange.rs:846 — no builder/schema/applier; F2a all net-new). `message.*` never mutates `SpaceState` node-side (`_ => Ok(())` state.rs:655 — the node's erasure job is the blob-delete; the display tombstone is client-side). `BlobStore` has **NO delete** (`new`/`put`/`get`/`contains` only, blob_store.rs:100/120/135/151 — `BlobStore::delete` is the load-bearing missing primitive). The author's `Retention` is reachable without new plumbing (`IdentityRecord.trust_assertion` registry.rs:45 → `module_policy().erasability.retention`), with **zero production `Retention` readers** (J-380/J-387 hold — F2b is M12's first). B caches federated blobs (`store.put(&bytes)` app.rs:1945 — a redact reaching B must delete B's cached copy). **No `blob_ref → events` reverse index exists** (the M12.3-audit finding holds — decisive for FK-8).

**Nine decisions Joe-LOCKED (M12.4-D1..D9, arc-local D-069 except D9).** **D1 (FK-1) redact schema = `{ target_event_id }` only** — the node resolves blob_refs from the target `message.file`'s descriptor (single source of truth); net-new builder + content shape. **D2 (FK-2, load-bearing, Joe-lock) F2b reads the ORIGINAL CONTENT AUTHOR's `Retention`** (the target message's sender), not the redactor's — per D-088/D-093 c2, retention is per-record: a Retained (T4) author's content can't be erased by anyone (including a lower-tier redactor), and a redactor can't elevate erasure power by being lower-tier; the *permission* to redact stays the separate, existing `SendMessages`/moderation gate. **D3 (FK-3, convergence spine, RED-on-revert) gate the SIDE-EFFECT, not admission** — the redact is always admitted/stored/fanned-out (a valid signed event); only the blob-erasure side-effect is `Retention`-gated (Retained → keep the bytes = legal-hold floor; Erasable/absent → delete); the display tombstone applies regardless; the INV-EXP/M8.6 lesson (tier-conditioned admission diverges, side-effect gates don't). **D4 (FK-4, exceeds the literal F2 "tombstone-only" lock, Joe-confirmed) tombstone AND delete-the-bytes** — tombstone the DAG event (the residue it can't erase — D3) + delete the blob bytes (the content it can erase now); F2a's spirit. **D5 (FK-5, mechanical) hook in `process_inbound`** after validate+store, sibling to M12.3's `BlobUploadEnd → store.put`; the runbook grounds the exact site. **D6 (FK-6) minimal client tombstone in M12.4** — a redacted message must not render its descriptor / fetch its blob (the user-visible witness); richer redaction UI deferred to UI. **D7 (FK-7, re-grep at build) reject/refusal codes in domain 10** — reserve **`10004 erasure_refused_retained`** (a typed `BlobError` variant, the M12-D9 parallel error type, not `ExchangeError`; mirrors M12.3's 10003) for the F2b refusal signal to the redactor; reuse existing codes for not-found/malformed; RC-F-01 re-grep the register before emitting. **D8 (FK-8 — SUPERSEDES the audit's scan/accept-the-hazard rec; resolved by D-093 c3) NO shared physical copy across erasure-fate** — the audit predates the T4-reasoning that produced D-093 c3. Reasoning: retention/erasability is per-record (D-093 c2); a single shared physical copy lets one record's policy silently override another's (a lower-tier erasure deleting bytes a T4 record holds = durability-floor breach; a T4 hold blocking a lower-tier record's valid erasure = right-to-erasure breach). A refcount/reverse-index manages shared-copy bookkeeping but **cannot resolve the tier collision** (can't honor "A held, B erasable" on one physical blob) — heavy AND insufficient. **Lock:** an attachment blob's physical copy may be shared only among references that share the same erasure-fate; **M12.4 v1 = no attachment dedup** (one physical copy per `message.file` send, each with its own deletable storage handle; the **content-hash retained as descriptor metadata**, not the storage key, so identical-file detection / policy-keyed dedup-within-a-shared-fate-set stays a future optimization — not a correctness fix); a redact deletes only that reference's own copy → the A-09 hazard can't arise. **Runbook-bound mechanism (grounded, not a Joe-lock):** how `blob_ref` is derived today (pure `hash(bytes)` doubling as the storage key?) decides clean-handle vs a small additive per-send-salt on the storage handle (content-hash stays pure for the metadata) — Clair grounds + picks; the invariant is the lock. **D9 (Joe-lock) M12-D6 PROMOTED → `DECISIONS.md` D-093.** Three bound clauses: (1) universal E2E / no protocol escrow; (2) "Retained (T4)" = ciphertext durability-floor + erasure-refusal, retain-and-produce reserved to the operator/module layer; (3) no shared physical blob copy across erasure-fate (the D8 corollary). M12.4 is the arc that first exercises it (D2/D3 = first enforcement read; D4/D8 = first mechanism); past the 3-recurrence bar (AH-D1 + D-088 lineage, carried J-381→J-387). M12-D6's design-doc flag flips to "promoted → D-093."

**Witnesses (M12.4; RED-on-revert; runbook firms).** WE1 blob-bytes erasure (redact → ciphertext gone from `blobs_dir` → fetch `10003`) · WE2 F2b Retained refusal (Retained author → bytes kept + `10004`; Erasable/absent → deleted; first `Retention` reader) · WE3 convergence (redact stored + fanned identically regardless of side-effect outcome) · WE4 federated erasure (B deletes its cached copy on the redact) · WE5 shared-fate safety (identical bytes → two physical copies → redact one, the other untouched) · WE6 D3 boundary (close-claim: M12.4 erases bytes + refuses-on-Retained + tombstones, NOT the DAG-residue crypto-shred — that's D3).

**Canonical (D-074).** audit `tasks/M12_4_ERASURE_PHASE0_AUDIT.md` (Clair, `31e17aa`, pushed); design doc NEW `tasks/M12_4_ERASURE_DESIGN.md` (v1.0 ACTIVE); **`DECISIONS.md` D-093 NEW** (the M12-D6 promotion, three clauses); `CLAUDE.md` PLAY head (M12.4 design-lock, live head); `docs/ROADMAP.md` **v3.76→v3.77** (M12.4 opened + designed at tree / chain / detail; M12-D6 → promoted); this JOURNAL J-388; `tasks/M12_ATTACHMENTS_DESIGN.md` M12-D6 flag → "promoted → D-093." **No Appendix F** (no CLI verb/flag changed at the design-lock; the redact verb — if the runbook adds one — carries its 4-arm D-092 + Appendix F obligations at impl).

**Next-active: Clair authors the M12.4 runbook** (`tasks/M12_4_*_IMPL.md`, the §3 scope, spine-first — re-grounds the anchors, grounds the `blob_ref` derivation + picks the D8 mechanism, picks the `10004` variant, defines the witness set) → Joe-lock the runbook values → implement spine-first, per-commit, Joe pushes each → Chat close-bridge → **M12.4 close = M12 close** → Round-2 final pre-UI gate → UI → Streams. No code until the M12.4 runbook lands + Joe-locks. **Entry (Rule 0): CLAUDE.md PLAY → JOURNAL J-388 → `tasks/M12_4_ERASURE_DESIGN.md` → `tasks/M12_4_ERASURE_PHASE0_AUDIT.md` → `tasks/M12_ATTACHMENTS_DESIGN.md` (M12-D6/D10) → `DECISIONS.md` D-093/D-088/AH-D1 → `docs/ROADMAP.md` (M12).** Not pushed — Joe pushes.

## Entry J-387 — M12.3 SHIPPED + CLOSED: federation fetch-blob-by-hash (D1 β-multiplex / D4 sync / D5 typed 10003); box-gated e2e green; next-active = M12.4 (erasure)

**What happened.** Clair implemented M12.3 spine-first across three commits on top of the runbook `e24bef9`; Joe pushed; the box-gated real-binary two-home e2e RUN went green; Chat cross-verified on `main` (D-065) and landed this close bridge. M12.3 — federation **fetch-blob-by-hash** — is **SHIPPED + CLOSED**. HEAD `709811f`, tree clean, in sync with origin.

**What shipped (the D1 β multiplex, taken head-on per audit A-02).** The `message.file` descriptor already federates (eager push); the **bytes** did not — the federation steady-state loop dropped blob `TransportMessage`s on its `Ok(_)` catch-all. M12.3 closes that gap: on a client↔node fetch **miss**, home B resolves the Space's federated holders (`home_node ∪ federation_nodes ∩ live sessions`, home_node-first, **serialize-one-fetch-per-peer** — P2, no `BlobChunk` wire change) and fetches the ciphertext **across homes over the established federation session** (no new conn, no re-handshake): an `OutboundMsg::BlobFetchRequest` injector + a shared **`PendingFederationFetches = Arc<Mutex<HashMap<NodeXgid, FetchSlot>>>`** registry (forced by `OutboundMsg: #[derive(Clone)]`, V5 — a `oneshot` can't ride a Clone enum). The federation loop gained **serve + collect + inject arms ahead of the `Ok(_)` catch-all** (the clean arm-add the design predicted — no Event-ordering entanglement; blob fetch/reply is its own request/response, concurrent with the Event push), threaded through both session-driver chains (receiver + reconnect-initiator) + the in-process harness. B serves the bytes (cached content-blind) or the typed **`10003 blob_unavailable`** on unreachable/timeout (D4 **synchronous**: B blocks the client fetch during the round-trip; inner timeout = `[sync].completion_timeout_seconds` 5s, outer client `fetch_blob` 2× — P3). `space_id` rides as an **additive `Option`** on the wire `BlobFetchRequest` (no existing-caller break — P1).

**Commits (spine-first, per-commit DoD-gated).** runbook `e24bef9` · **C1** `9a2332d` — type the `10003` reject (D5): `BlobError::Unavailable` → `to_wire_code` `Some((10003, "blob_unavailable"))` (blob_store.rs:86), replacing the defensive literal at app.rs:1919 (W2 baseline; byte-identical wire) · **C2** `df053f7` — the federation fetch path (D1/D4, the spine bulk) + the in-process spine witness · **C3** `709811f` — the box-gated real-binary two-home e2e (W1 headline, `#[ignore]`, sibling to `m12_2a_self_thread_e2e`). **DoD each:** build 0-error · clippy `--all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean · in-suite `cargo test --workspace` → **1448/0** (1445 baseline + C1 unit + C2's two in-process witnesses; the e2e `#[ignore]` keeps the in-suite count unchanged). **RED-on-revert recorded:** C1 (drop the `to_wire_code` arm → fails) + C2 (neuter the collect arm → W1 `Err(())`, restored to green).

**Grounding confirmation (D-065, J-381).** Arc-H text encryption is universal E2E with no escrow / no tier-conditioning / no recovery key: zero escrow/tier/retention hits across `xgen-core/src/encryption/`, and the defended invariant `erasing_wrapped_key_defeats_epoch_holder` (AH-D1 constraint 2, `client_mls.rs`) makes the per-message content key random and never epoch-derived — destroying the wrapped CK is permanent even for the epoch holder. **Ten decisions Joe-LOCKED (M12-D1..D10, arc-local D-069 unless marked).** **D1** pipe byte-transfer = **chunked base64** (the gate, M12-A-01) — a net-new transfer sub-protocol *inside* the existing text-line model (base64-chunked bounded lines + begin/size/sentinel framing, symmetric upload/fetch); chosen over length-prefixed binary (breaks the UTF-8-line invariant both pipe surfaces depend on) and single-field base64 (multi-MB single line + whole-file-in-memory, a later reshape against F1). **D2** message seam = **reuse `message.file`** (already validation-wired; no new event kind = the F5 answer; `file.upload`/`message.attachment-meta` doc-only; `stream.*`/`media.*` clean doc reservation); build the missing `build_message_file_event` carrying `attachments: [Descriptor]` (F1 plural; rides DAG+fanout like `message.text`, no `SpaceState` apply arm). **D3** net-new **`Descriptor`** = `blob_ref` (ciphertext hash = content-address / store key) + `plaintext_hash` (post-decrypt integrity) + `key` (per-blob) + `filename`/`mime`/`size`, carried **inside** the `enc:` E2E content. **D4** **blob store** = content-addressed `blobs_dir` `PathsSection` sibling, default `<data_dir>/blobs` (events + referenced blobs back up / snapshot / tier as one unit — the T4 requirement); content-blind (ciphertext only); `EventStore` untouched (event-only). **D5** blob encryption = **same Arc-H envelope as text** (fresh per-blob key → encrypt → upload ciphertext; node content-blind, content-addresses by ciphertext hash; key + plaintext-hash ride the descriptor inside `enc:`; same group reads text + blob, no new key distribution). *Flag 1:* inherits the text path's D3 crypto maturity (demonstration-grade now; production RFC 9420 HPKE = the M8.7 S+L openmls arc) — interface now, prod crypto when text's D3 lands; not stronger/weaker than text. **D6 (DECISIONS.md PROMOTION CANDIDATE)** E2E philosophy = **universal at the protocol layer** — every tier crypto-shreddable, **no protocol escrow key** (grounded above). ## Entry J-379 — M12 (attachments) OPENED: concept + Phase-0 scope + forks F1–F9 Joe-LOCKED; next-active = Clair D-071 Phase-0 audit

**What happened.** M12 opened cold (M11 closed at J-378; `main` clean, tree green 1405/0). **Provenance grounded (D-065, J-379).** J-357 was a planning lock (existence + placement), not a scope lock. Grep of `main`: **no blob store today** (event-only `EventStore` over a SQLite `events` table — every "blob" hit is MLS / Arc-H content-blindness); **§3.1.1's size model is envelope-only and mostly unwired** (only the 256 KB frame ceiling enforced; the per-tier table + Space `max_event_size` are spec/stored-but-not-enforced); **`ModulePolicy`** (`claims.extra["module_policy"]`, `erasability` first member) is the dormant extensible switch-bag with **zero production readers**; `file.upload` / `message.attachment-meta` are event-kind breadcrumbs.

**Concept Joe-LOCKED.** Metadata-by-value / content-by-reference: the event carries a **descriptor** (hash + name + mime + size); the bytes live in a **net-new content-addressed blob store**. Bytes never ride the event — three structural reasons: the §3.1.1 size ceiling; the immutable signed DAG (`event_id` = hash of the event's bytes); erasability impossibility + federation cost. **Send = upload-and-persist** to the home node (not link-to-source, not Skype-style direct device→device) — the source device is irrelevant after upload, download needs no second device online. The **`self` thread is M12's front door**: intra-home multi-device sharing rides blob store + pipe upload + pipe fetch and **never touches federation**, so M11/D-021's never-federated guarantee stays intact; it is the headline witness for M12.1.

**Nine forks Joe-LOCKED (F1–F9, arc-local D-069).** **F1** descriptor = a multi-file list from day one (`attachments: [Descriptor]`; schema plural, build single-first if useful). **F2** GDPR/deletion = **F2a** tombstone-only lean (inherit the Arc-I shape + D-088 + AI-D8 erasability; ## Entry J-363 — M10.2 design Joe-LOCKED: offline-token issuance + live-read registry→policy + config-seed; accepted_tiers deferred to M10.3; next-active = Clair runbook

**What happened.** Clair's M10.2 Phase-0 audit landed (`629b30c`, `tasks/M10_2_REFERENCE_BINARY_AUDIT.md` v1.0, grounded vs `main` @`a86db48`, 5 findings, hash-typo self-caught + fixed). Chat verified it, framed the four shape calls the audit surfaced, and Joe locked them (by-recomms). Chat authored the design doc `tasks/M10_2_REFERENCE_BINARY_DESIGN.md` (v1.0 ACTIVE). Doc-only; no code; no DECISIONS change (M10.2-D# arc-local, D-069).

**Audit headline (frame holds, sharpened).** The trust-source change is a **single seam**: one production caller of `validate_assertion` (`registration.rs:486` via `accept_registration`), one node path (`handle_identity_msg`, `app.rs:2842`); the gate's trust set is a startup config snapshot (`app.rs:745–749`), disconnected from the CRUD registry. The binary is an **offline signer** (`endpoint_url` is only the `auth-module test` probe target — the node verifies the presented signature offline, never calls the module). Spec-aligned: §3016 step-1 says the issuer must be a registered Auth Module per §3.8.7 — the registry *is* that store, so (b) registry→policy is more spec-aligned than the config seam.

**Four decisions Joe-LOCKED.**
- **M10.2-D1 — issuance = offline-signed token.** Binary signs a Tier-1 `TrustAssertion` (issuer = `AuthModuleXgid::from_pubkey(pk).to_string()`, signed with the module key — the synthetic test issuer's exact shape); identity attaches it to register; node verifies offline. No live endpoint. Challenge/response = flagged future.
- **M10.2-D2 — trust source = `AuthModuleRegistry`, live-read; registry to `run_node` top-level.** Gate flips from the config snapshot to a live registry read at validation time; the `Arc<Mutex<AuthModuleRegistry>>` moves to `run_node` top-level (shared gate + CRUD) — the **first runtime consumer, structurally closing AMR-D1**; `revoke` bites immediately, no restart. `register`/`revoke` enforcement-bearing.
- **M10.2-D3 — config `trusted_auth_modules` bootstrap-seeds the registry: add-only + idempotent + revoke-wins.** Seed inserts only-if-absent, re-runs safely, never un-revokes a CRUD-revoked issuer (operator revoke authoritative). **Prime invariant:** empty config + empty registry = today byte-for-byte (baseline/`local_mode` untouched, Fork 1).
- **M10.2-D4 — `accepted_tiers` enforcement deferred to M10.3.** M10.2 ships trust on/off + live revoke (all T1 needs); the per-issuer tier check is a `validate_assertion` shape change with nothing to enforce until T2–T4 exist (M10.3, the mock, which can witness it). **Narrows the literal M10-A-02 wording on *timing* only; the (b) direction is untouched. M10.3 owns making accepted_tiers enforcement-bearing** (recorded, not dropped).
- **M10.2-D5 — the binary = pure offline signer (M10-A-06).** Reuses `keypair.rs` (generate/save/load, encrypt-at-rest); own keypair; signs T1 assertions as itself; **populates the M10.1 descriptor** (`module_kind: reference` + `module_policy.erasability`); operator registers it via the existing CRUD; no module-presented manifest.

**Honesty items accepted (audit A5):** `SignedPrimitive` is a **concept, not a trait** (the design wording reflects it); T1 verification = **proof-of-key-possession** only (the issuance logic is honest about what it attests).

**Proof obligations (RED-on-revert, Clair builds):** (1) end-to-end accept (module issues → identity registers → node validates against registry-trusted issuer → accept; extends `non_local_registration_with_valid_assertion_accepted`); (2) **live revoke** rejects without restart (proves D2 live-read); (3) config-seed honoured + idempotent + revoke-wins; (4) **empty-baseline invariant** (empty+empty = today).

**Canonical flips (D-074).** `tasks/M10_2_REFERENCE_BINARY_DESIGN.md` NEW (v1.0 ACTIVE); `CLAUDE.md` PLAY head; `docs/ROADMAP.md` v3.52→v3.53 (M10 detail M10.2-design annotation + M-series/chain markers M10.2-PHASE-0 → M10.2-DESIGN); this JOURNAL J-363. No DECISIONS change.

**Next-active: Clair** — author `tasks/M10_2_REFERENCE_BINARY_IMPL.md` (the `xgen-auth-module` binary crate + the trust-source rewire + registry relocation to `run_node` top-level + the config-seed + the four witnesses), confirming the §3 groundings + the §5 design-close details to file:line → implement → Chat doc-bridge → close. The one detail to surface if non-obvious: the live-read shape at the gate (§5). ## Entry J-362 — M10.2 OPENED (Tier-1 reference binary `xgen-auth-module`): two calls Joe-locked (M10-A-02 = registry→policy wiring; M10-A-06 = operator-CRUD); Phase-0 brief authored; next-active = Clair D-071 audit

**What happened.** With M10.1 closed (J-361), Joe opened M10.2 — the second M10 sub-arc and the **first with a real new binary**. **Goal.** Ship `xgen-auth-module` — a separate binary, own keypair, that **issues** Tier-1 `TrustAssertion`s (signs them as itself) so an identity can present a real (non-synthetic) module-signed assertion at registration and drive the live 7-check `validate_assertion` end-to-end against a registry-trusted issuer. Turns the shipped foundation from *dormant-but-correct* into *demonstrated* (Fork 1: a demonstrator over the hardcoded baseline, floor untouched).

**Two calls Joe-LOCKED.**
- **M10-A-02 (spine) = (b) wire registry → policy.** `validate_assertion` consults `AuthModuleRegistry` as the trust source; `register`/`revoke`/`accepted_tiers` become enforcement-bearing (closes the AMR-D1 standalone-no-consumer deferral). Rejected (a) status-quo config seam — it leaves the two disconnected surfaces + ships a `revoke` that doesn't revoke. **Config-seed sub-lock:** `[node].trusted_auth_modules` is neither deprecated nor a second live source — at startup it **bootstrap-seeds the registry** (migration-free; existing config trust keeps working) and the gate reads the registry. Seed-vs-CRUD precedence = a design-lock detail.
- **M10-A-06 = operator-CRUD kept.** The trust decision stays operator-controlled (a module self-asserting trust would break the `trusted_auth_modules` safety model). The binary is a pure **signer + issuance endpoint**; operator registers it via the existing 5 CRUD verbs. A module-presented manifest/handshake is a **flagged future enhancement**, not M10.2.

**Out (explicit):** M10.3 the T2–T4 mock + dormant-tier-path activation; M10.4 MP-F13; a module-presented manifest (flagged); erasure *enforcement* (the `module_policy.erasability` consumer stays D3-gated — M10.1 landed only the field).

**What the Phase-0 audit must ground (brief §3, to file:line):** the **issuance path** (challenge/response vs offline-signed vs operator-mediated; what the synthetic test issuer does today + the exact `TrustAssertion` shape to produce); the **Call-1b trust-source seam** (`app.rs:746` config → `AssertionPolicy.trusted_issuers` `registration.rs:200`; the minimal change to read `AuthModuleRegistry` + where the startup config-seed lands); **`AuthModuleRecord`/`endpoint_url` semantics** (does the node ever *call* the module, or only verify the presented assertion's signature against the trusted issuer pubkey — i.e. is the binary an offline signer or a live endpoint in M10.2); the **keypair/signing surface** (`SignedPrimitive` canonical-bytes signer; `AuthModuleXgid`, D-083); **what "Tier-1 verification" means in code** (likely proof-of-key-possession only); and confirm the binary **populates the M10.1 descriptor** (`module_kind: reference` + `module_policy.erasability`) on issued assertions. D-065/D-078 guardrails apply — if grounding contradicts a locked call, surface + re-lock.

(b) each leaf post gets a stable id `p{i}` **gated on its own join landing**: the join now exports `a{i}_joined` (its `event_id`), carried in an **inert gate field** the node binary tolerates (grounded: `Command` has no `deny_unknown_fields`), and the harness blocks on the `{{a{i}_joined}}` token — so the leaf post is real post-join cross-node content, not a post racing its own join. Design-fidelity notes (surfaced): `EventRecord`/`Transcript` carry `event_id`, not message text, so presence is keyed by `event_id`; the cross-actor gating reuses the existing exports + `{{key}}` registry primitives, so no `GeneratedTemplate` extension was needed and the `StarPlusMesh` generator path stayed untouched.

Federation_nodes were correct + delivery happened → Fork A/B off-target. **Actual root:** p0 arrives on n1 and is **HeldPending for a missing causal predecessor** (the F-4a buffer, `runtime.rs:1193`) that never drains. p0's `prev_events` = the `get_dag_tips` frontier (`xgen-client/src/batch.rs:96`, the MP-F4/J-331 fix): 5 tips = 3 `membership.join` + `state.room_create` + one **`state.federation_add`** — a **vantage-specific / directional (D-075)** infra event that never converges to n1 (the oracle excludes it via `INFRA_EVENT_KINDS`, MP-R1-D7, which is why the verdict flags only p0). A cooperative message anchored to a non-converging infra predecessor → un-applyable → permanent miss. The ~60% intermittency = the race on whether a `state.federation_add` is a frontier tip at p0's `after_ms:40` send; `compute_frontier` does not filter by kind. **The MP-F4/J-331 causal-frontier family** — MP-F4 widened `get_dag_tips` to the full frontier (room-join anchoring); that same frontier now over-anchors cooperative content to non-converging infra.

**Re-locked fix (MP-F14-D2 supersedes Fork A; Joe-confirmed).** Exclude infra kinds (`state.federation_add`) from the cooperative frontier `get_dag_tips` returns for a new cooperative event's `prev_events`, so DAG-anchoring **agrees with** the convergence contract. **Kind pinned by observation = (b) a real leave→rejoin convergence fault.** Phase-0 grounded the three candidates against the live DAG + replies. **(a) FALSIFIED** — `ops::leave` doesn't touch `ClientState.spaces`; `members` re-derives from node-drained events (not a cached client view), so a1's empty `members` reply is *downstream* of a1 being a non-member, not a dropped cache. **(c) NOT-root** — the oracle correctly flagged genuine non-convergence: a0's authoritative view resolves `members = {a0:owner}`, a1 genuinely absent. **(b) CONFIRMED + sharpened — the DAG smoking gun:** the rejoin `rj` is anchored to the `space_create` root (`prev=[space_create]`), making it **concurrent** with the leave `lv` on the membership key `membership:{space}:a1`; `derive_resolved` resolves the `{leave, rejoin}` frontier and **leave wins** (deterministic Layer-1 leave>join priority, algorithm.rs:105/146-147) → a1 stays a non-member; the `members`=None reply is then downstream (a non-member's member-gated sync starves it of history). **Root:** `ops::join`'s `get_dag_tips` falls back to `vec![space_id]` (the root) when the just-left non-member's member-gated sync returns no tips — the leave anchored to a real tip (a1 was still a member then), so the asymmetry is the pin. Mechanically the **MP-F4/J-331 family** (a membership event dropped because bad `prev_events` made it concurrent). A real protocol/client fault — any user who leaves then rejoins an open Space stays a non-member — not a test artifact; engine-sound (MP-C-05 ran the identical sweep/oracle/derive machinery green-to-8; its actors never leave, so never hit the rejoin-anchoring path).

**Fix = Fork A, client-side causal anchoring (C1 `8358bb5`).** The open rejoiner must anchor its join after its own leave, not the root. A `ClientState.last_local_events` map (`space_id → event_id`) — **separate** from `KnownSpace` by design (the wrinkle Joe locked: the anchor is causal-DAG bookkeeping, not membership state, so it lives outside the joined-list → zero `whoami`/`spaces` pollution, zero consumer sweep, additive D-077 surface). `ops::leave` persists the leave's event_id; `ops::join` reads it on the `get_dag_tips`-empty fallback so the rejoin descends from its own leave (linear `j→lv→rj` → `frontier_of={rj}` → a1 member). **Best-effort by design:** an absent/stale anchor degrades to the root (first-join unchanged, old `state.json` loads) — the presence-check is both the rejoin-vs-first-join distinguisher and the safety fallback; a missing anchor never errors. **Fork B** (node scoped-fetch for an open rejoiner) declined as primary — it widens the member-gated-sync boundary (the J-333 "unconditional skip would be a hole" surface) for no benefit over A. **Fork C** (resolution tiebreak: rejoin beats leave) rejected outright — would break ban/kick dominance; resolution must never infer intent from concurrent membership events. (Clair's check that the Layer-1 leave>join priority is *deterministic* is what makes the RED-witness non-flaky **and** confirms Fork C is wrong — changing that tiebreak breaks the spec'd priority.)

**D-076 spine proven, not assumed (the centerpiece, framed against the MP-F4 falsification).** MP-F4's A1-as-locked was falsified mid-arc because separating the keys didn't *order* the joins — the real fix was the causal edge. The same lesson is the spine here, so it was proven before the client fix: two xgen-core `derive_resolved` tests, RED-on-revert genuine via the two DAG shapes — `..._rejoin_anchored_after_leave_is_member` ✓ (`rj=[lv]` → linear → a1 member) + `..._rejoin_anchored_at_root_is_dropped` ✓ (`rj=[root]` → concurrent → leave elected → a1 non-member), across orderings, no new concurrency manufactured. The causal edge is demonstrably load-bearing.

**Witness: MP-C-11 GREEN-on-rerun.** The box-gated churn-sweep ran 4 rungs (2→8 clients), `break_point=None` — all rungs converge GREEN, **including the rung-0 floor that was the deterministic LogicFault**. ## Entry J-345 — MP-F9 Phase-0 ✅ + design ✅ Joe-LOCKED: late-fed backfill gap PINNED = PROTOCOL (bounded — events backfill, identities don't); terminal-state A (fix-in-fix-phase, conditional); design-locked F9-D1/D2/D3 + F10-D1; next-active = MP-F9 implementation runbook (exec step 1 = confirming re-run)

**What happened.** The MP-R2 fix-phase opened on its first gate item, MP-F9 (the C3 late-federation backfill RED). Clair ran the D-071 Phase-0 + design phase; Joe locked the verdict (PROTOCOL, bounded) and the terminal-state (A — fix-in-fix-phase, conditional). This entry = the Chat verdict + design-lock doc-bridge. Clair's audit (`dcfc81a`) + design arc-docs are hers (committed/committing FIRST); this bridge second. This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

**Date:** 2026-06-11

**Kind verdict: PROTOCOL (bounded) — grounded, decisive.** Phase-0 (`tasks/MP_F9_LATE_FEDERATION_BACKFILL_AUDIT.md`) traced the late-fed RED to a precise cause, not a vague capability hole. The federation backfill path **exists and is correct sender-side**: A's `stream_federation_delta` fires its absent-peer rule for a peer-with-no-events, `compute_federation_delta_for_space(None)` returns the full topo-sorted history, and A's `shared_spaces` (incl. the late Space) is threaded through — A streams `[space_create, room_create, message, federation_add]` to B. B **holds all of it**, and the decisive datum is the symptom being *zero* events, not "only `state.space_create`": `space_create` skips the F-3 gate (`runtime.rs:1027-1032`), so the only thing that holds the create too is **step-11 sender-registration** — `StateSpaceCreate` is NOT in the `node_authored` exempt set (`exchange.rs:622-633`), so an alice-signed create with alice unknown to B → `HeldPending(missing_identity=alice)`. Every backfilled event is alice-signed → all held → empty transcript (uniquely explains the symptom). **Root: late federation backfills the events but NOT the identities that signed them** — `push_identity_to_peers` fires only at registration to then-current peers (`app.rs:2856/3118-3192`), and the federation session streams Space-DAG events only, never the registry. A peer joining a network that already has history+identities catches up the events but can't validate them. So this is a **bounded PROTOCOL gap**, not "no late-federation backfill exists."

**Terminal-state A (fix-in-fix-phase) — the fix composes via existing machinery.** Design (`tasks/MP_F9_LATE_FEDERATION_BACKFILL_DESIGN.md`) confirmed the fix-vs-route question lands on A: (1) `handle_identity_replicate_msg` already auto-fires `drain_pending_by_identity` on a record landing (`app.rs:2913/2975`, `runtime.rs:1717`), releasing exactly the F-10-held events for that signer, in the same lock — land the signer's record on B and the held backfill drains automatically; no new wire message / receive handler / drain logic. (2) **Disclosure is already settled** (the D5-non-drag): establish already `record_peer_url`s the peer "to push identity replicas later" (`app.rs:1976-1983`), and `push_identity_to_peers` already serializes the whole `IdentityRecord` (incl. `home_node`) to peers at registration (`app.rs:3135`) — so an early-federated peer already receives later-registered members' full records. The late-fed fix replicates *the same records, same category, different trigger*. It is **NOT** MP-F1b's D5 (stranger home-node discovery) — B is catching up records of signers whose events it's already receiving. The ONLY gap is the trigger.

**Design-locked decisions.** **F9-D1** — a backlog-push on federation-establish (both sides, symmetric), reusing the existing send-path. **F9-D2** — the trigger generalizes to any establish; the reconnect path is the same code the late-fed initiate uses (J-085), so R3/MP-A-08 (partition+reconnect) reuses it for free. **F9-D3** — signer-set = the **distinct senders of the backfilled delta**, NOT current-members-only (R3-correct: a reconnecting peer must validate historical events whose signers may have since left; the members-only shortcut is wrong). **MP-F10 (carried, independent): F10-D1** — a dependency-ordered single-owner director, ordering steps by publish→wait edges (the clock step publishing `clock_advanced` runs before the fed link waiting on it), staying sequential + preserving the `&mut nodes` single-owner model → no deadlock. Rides the F9 implementation (same C3 machinery). Row coupling: MP-F9 gates **both** C3 rows; F10-D1 additionally unblocks the clock-aged Smoke 2 (`mp_a_01_ii`).

**Conditional terminal-A (D-065 honesty).** Terminal-A holds *iff* the confirming traced re-run nails the verdict (the `state.space_create` HeldPending is the discriminator) and implementation surfaces no real disclosure-scoping fork the registration-precedent doesn't already cover. If the re-run contradicts the trace, or a genuine disclosure fork appears → it reverts to **route-to-R3-as-named-dependency** (coherent; R3/MP-A-08 needs identity-catch-up anyway). A locked terminal-state is a strong default, not a muzzle. **Honest boundary:** the verdict is by code-trace + the unique zero-event explanation — **no live instrumented re-run yet** (box-gated). This is a **production-crate protocol fix** (xgen-node + the receive path) — full arc discipline, no code until the runbook is Joe-locked.

**Sequencing (ii, Joe-locked):** the runbook is authored now (the code-trace verdict is strong enough to design against), with the **confirming traced re-run as runbook execution step 1** — nothing ships before it confirms. The re-run is box-gated (coordinate with Joe); it gates the fix, not the authoring.

Cause: the `cargo test --workspace` regression-check step rebuilt `xgen-node.exe` with default features, clobbering the `harness-control` binary at the pinned target dir (`C:/cargo-targets/XGenProtocol/debug`). Rebuilt harness-control → targeted C7 re-run (no re-clobber) → 7/7 against the correct fenced binary. Joe locked F-RU-1..4 by recommendation, with the F-RU-1 wholesale-replace documentation add (RU-D1). This entry = the Chat doc-bridge (matrix MP-C-08 → ✅ + §6 recount, DECISIONS +D-092, MP_findings +MP-F6, PLAY/JOURNAL/ROADMAP); commit order honoured (Clair's two commits precede this). This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

**Date:** 2026-06-10

**The verb (thin, as scoped).** Client `room_update` over the already-shipped `build_room_update_event` + `apply_room_update` + the `check_permission` per-room override gate — client verb only, mirrors `create_room` + ban's send-confirm, wire-neutral (the overrides ride signed `content`; the builder shipped in Arc D PG-12-min). The applier **replaces the room's complete override set wholesale** (Arc D CP-3 — present array = full set, empty clears, absent untouched). Verb-add surface = clap `RoomUpdateArgs` + `ops::room_update` (→ `apply_single_event_confirm`, the MP-F5 site) + `cmd_room_update` shim + **4 dispatch arms** (main CLI / app run-path / batch / aicontrol) — all four applied up front (the ban lesson; no `UNKNOWN_COMMAND` surprise this arc).

**Pre-fold gate cleared (the precondition class that bit ban/auth-tier).** Chat flagged at lock that the witness seats bob "as moderator" and that this had to be grounded, not assumed — if `invite` were member/admin-only the witness would need a promote path and the arc would no longer be thin. Clair grounded it: `Role::from_str("moderator") → Some(Moderator)`; `apply_invite` parses `content["role"]` via `Role::from_str` (state.rs:965) and `apply_join` seats the member at the invited role (state.rs:1006). So `invite --role moderator` seats Moderator directly — arc stays thin, no promote path.

**PG-12 has teeth.** `check_permission` (exchange.rs:820–833) returns `PermissionDenied` on a `Deny` override during `validate_event`, unit-proven by the flagship "Moderators can't post in #announcements" (exchange.rs:2464). "No-op today" only for lack of an authoring verb (the PG-13 parallel) — this arc removes exactly that blocker → MP-C-08 green-eligible, no finding routed.

**Four forks Joe-locked (by recommendation).** F-RU-1 `--deny <role>:<perm>` + `--allow <role>:<perm>` (repeatable `Vec<String>`, single-value-per-flag — works with the harness `reconstruct_argv`, which a JSON-array value does not), applier replaces wholesale; **+ the binding RU-D1 add (Chat, D-065):** because wholesale-replace on a production verb silently wipes unlisted overrides, the semantics are stated **explicitly** in both the `RoomUpdateArgs` help text and the Appendix F entry ("sets the room's COMPLETE override set; unlisted overrides cleared"). F-RU-2 oracle asserts **both** halves. F-RU-3 single-node (the override-honored property is node-local). F-RU-4 witness `(Moderator, SendMessages, Deny)`, bob seated moderator (the flagship).

**MP-C-08 ✅ (`mp_r1_c5`).** alice creates S + room1 (open) + room2 (carries the override) → `room_update room2 --deny moderator:send_messages` → invites bob as moderator → bob joins both → bob posts in both. **Positive / per-room independence:** room1 post (no override) accepted + converges; the `(Moderator, SendMessages)→Deny` override present in room2's resolved state. **Enforcement (assert-the-reject, the MP-F5 inheritance):** bob's room2 post routes through `ops::send` → `apply_single_event_confirm` (the MP-F5 site) → `reject_code=4000` (PermissionDenied — an unmapped variant, **pinned to observed** per the MP-A-20 precedent; MP-F2-followon) + `event_id`, the post absent everywhere. RED-on-revert genuine: neuter `ops::room_update` to author no overrides → room2 has no Deny → bob's room2 post accepted (Ok) → the enforcement assert flips RED; restored → GREEN.

**4-dispatch-arm rule promoted → D-092.** The verb-add surface = clap struct + ops + CLI shim + **four** dispatch arms (main CLI · app run-path · batch · **aicontrol `Box::pin`**). The aicontrol arm is the silent-miss path: it returns `UNKNOWN_COMMAND` over `--aicontrol` (the path the mptest harness drives) while manual CLI testing passes. Caught empirically on ban (J-337), applied up front + confirmed inert-of-surprises here — a global, repeatable, silently-biting xgen-client rule, so promoted from arc-doc candidate to a DECISIONS entry. Binds thread×3 + every future verb-add.

**runtime.rs:691 breadcrumb routed → MP-F6 (low-sev, M10).** The ban arc surfaced (J-337) that `dispatch_event` swallows a join apply-error (`let _ =`) and has no `banned` pre-check — benign for MP-A-14 (resolution drops the inert re-join) but the same swallowed-apply-error shape as MP-F5's class. Joe's standing desk-item (route now vs leave for R1-rerun) resolved by recommendation: **route now** as a named low-sev finding (MP-F6), deferred-fix tagged M10, so the seam is tracked rather than implicit. Not an R1-rerun blocker.

**Verification (actual, Clair).** Build 0 + clippy clean (default + `--all-features`); full fast suite 0-failed; MP-C-08 heavy GREEN; RED-on-revert confirmed; Appendix F gains the `room_update` entry with the wholesale-replace note (J-323 close-deliverable).

**Loop-to-green progress (MP-R1-D10):** MP-F2 ✅ → MP-F3 ✅ → MP-F1a ✅ → MP-F4 ✅ → MP-F1b ✅ → auth-tier ✅ → MP-F5 ✅ → ban ✅ → **room_update ✅ (J-338)** → thread×3 → R1 rerun. **DECISIONS change: +D-092** (4-dispatch-arm rule). `docs/tests/MULTIPARTY_TEST_MATRIX.md` v1.9→v1.10 (MP-C-08 → ✅ + the §6 status roll-up recount, which had drifted stale since Round-0). `tasks/MP_findings.md` v1.9→v1.10 (no room_update defect — arc-local; +MP-F6, the routed runtime.rs:691 breadcrumb). ROADMAP v3.27→v3.28. **Commit order (standing): Clair's code FIRST, then Chat's doc-bridge** — honoured (`d3adb41` + `70a80a6` precede this). **Next-active: Clair — thread×3 (arc 4, the last + biggest thin-verb arc — `thread.create`/`.resolved`/`.archived`, unblocks MP-C-13, rides M8 Layer-5c).** Phase-0 grounds: 4 arms per verb (D-092) + one-clap-subcommand-vs-three-verbs · the Arc E `auth_tier_min`/participation gate teeth · MP-C-13 oracle (positive Layer-5c `thread.status` convergence vs any unauthorized/non-participant reject-surfacing half) · single-node vs cross-node. **Entry point (Rule 0): CLAUDE PLAY → JOURNAL J-338 → `tasks/ROOM_UPDATE_VERB_DESIGN.md` → `docs/tests/MULTIPARTY_TEST_MATRIX.md` MP-C-13 row → `xgen-client/src/ops.rs` (verb-add pattern, all 4 arms / D-092).** This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

## Entry J-336 — MP-F5 SHIPPED (reject-surfacing + C6 oracle reconciliation; design 323fced + impl bee2ede): the client reply now carries the structured reject (code + event_id), the C6 oracle asserts-the-reject, MP-A-03 greens + A-02/04/17/20 re-grounded, MP-R1-D9 amended — record DEFERRED at ship time, folded into the J-337 doc-bridge

**Date:** 2026-06-10

**What MP-F5 was.** The favorable-direction close of the C6 reject-oracle finding (surfaced + routed at J-335): post-MP-F2/MP-F1a a locally-submitted reject already comes back as an `Error` frame carrying code + `event_id`; the client merely **flattened** it into anyhow free text. So MP-F5 = **finish the MP-F2 surfacing into the client reply**, not redesign the oracle. Five forks; Joe locked F2 (additive `ErrorBody` fields) + the category sub-fork (defer) + F4 (D-9 amendment) by recommendation; F1/F3/F5 design-settled.

**What shipped (`bee2ede`, single commit).** **F1** — `EventConfirm::Rejected` widened to carry `event_id` (the matched `sent_id` was already in hand); a typed `VerbReject` from `apply_single_event_confirm`; aicontrol downcasts it. One helper → all **8 single-event ops** inherit; `create_dm_space`'s multi-event chain left text-bailing (out of scope, no witness uses it). **F2 (Joe-locked)** — `ErrorBody` gains **additive** `reject_code: Option<u32>` + `event_id: Option<String>` (shipping envelope + harness mirror); `code=GENERIC_4000`/`category=Protocol` **retained** — the AC-D3d wall (a control-plane code can't represent a verb error) stays intact; a wire drift-lock test pins the JSON shape incl. the old-reader/absent case. **Category sub-fork DEFERRED** (Joe): `reject_code==3030` is a stronger, more precise assertion than a `category=Permission` remap, and a band→category table would walk into the open 3030-vs-3010 spec drift (MP-F2-followon) — the matrix's category-clause is satisfied by-stronger-means, not dropped. **F3** — the C6 oracle rewritten to **assert-the-reject** (`reject_code` present as a field + `event_id` + protected state unchanged + offending event absent), reading the harness `Reply::Error`/`.error()` that already existed. **F5** — the stale C6 tranche re-grounded.

**Empirical reject_codes (re-grounded against HEAD, per the "confirm don't assume" discipline — all assert-the-reject + paired):** MP-A-02 → **3045** (over-ceiling invite); MP-A-04 → **4000** (step-11 non-member); MP-A-17 → **4000** (space-not-found); MP-A-20 → **4000** (`can_invite` denial) — the three 4000s are unmapped variants pinned to observed (MP-F2-followon territory), each re-grounded from stale-PASS → ✅. **MP-A-03 → 3030** (tier_mismatch) — the auth-tier verb's deferred batch witness, **NEW ✅**: alice creates a Tier-2 Space, bob (Tier-1) refused at the PG-13 join-gate, join absent + bob not a member, converged; RED-on-revert genuine (flip the batch to `auth_tier:1` → bob joins → RED). The auth-tier verb's deferred half is retired here — no debt onto the R1 rerun.

**F4 — MP-R1-D9 amendment (Joe-blessed, scoped).** "Post-MP-F2 a **locally-submitted single-event reject IS batch-observable** — the node sends code + `event_id`, the client surfaces them structurally (`reject_code`/`event_id` fields), and the C6 oracle asserts the reject directly. The J-321 fire-and-forget / category-not-batch-observable premise is superseded **for that path**." Scoped deliberately to locally-submitted single-event rejects (the F1 path) — it does not over-claim for the multi-event chain or federated-reject paths. Recorded in `tasks/MP_R1_DETERMINISTIC_DESIGN.md` §10.

**Verification (Clair, actual).** C6 heavy tranche 5/5 GREEN; MP-A-03 RED-on-revert confirmed; fast suites green (xgen-core 689 · xgen-common 140 · xgen-client 103 · xgen-mptest 73 · xgen-node 286); clippy clean (default + `--all-features`); wire drift-lock test added; Appendix F §F.8 gains the reject-surfacing sibling note (J-323).

## Entry J-333 — MP-F1b SHIPPED + CLOSED (Design Z: parties-set + identity-replicate hook; F-3 intact, no skip); §3.2 "no new send code" falsified mid-arc by the live two-node witness (third arc this loop); MP-C-07 cross-node harness-green-with-boundary; invariant E promoted D-091; next-active = Clair (the 4 thin verbs)

**What happened.** MP-F1b shipped + closed (Clair — code + arc docs, commit `9b4ab8b`). The arc did NOT go straight from the J-332 design to ship: at C2 the live two-node MP-C-07 witness **falsified the design's §3.2 premise** ("the moment federation_nodes is populated the existing push path federates both directions, no new send code"), the F1B-D8 spine came back falsified, Option C was grounded absent, and Joe re-locked **Design Z** (the unifying fix). Chat doc-only follow (this entry): MP_findings MP-F1b → Z-shipped/CLOSED (v1.7), MP-C-07 matrix row → harness-green-with-boundary (v1.7), invariant E promoted to **D-091**, arc docs AUDIT/DESIGN(v1.1)/IMPL(v1.1) → COMPLETED, this PLAY/JOURNAL/ROADMAP. Commit order: Clair's code (`9b4ab8b`) pushed FIRST, then this doc-bridge. This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

**Date:** 2026-06-09

**The mid-arc correction (D-065, the arc's standout — the third such this loop: MP-F3 gate-placement, MP-F4 fold-order, now MP-F1b receiving-side).** The J-332 design locked (iii)/F1B-D1..D7 with §3.2 asserting the helper alone flips MP-C-07 ("no new send code"). Clair built C1 (the helper + 4 apply-site hooks + 4 units, all green in isolation) then ran the live two-node witness — which **advanced past the old KNOWN-FAIL but stayed RED**: bob's join applied on B, alice's view on A stayed `{alice}`. Surfaced, not worked around; grounded empirically (a file-logged member→home diagnostic surviving the harness temp-dir cleanup, + the MP-C-02 baseline as contrast).

**Two receiving-side gaps + a third timing dependency — one root cause.** The in-process units couldn't see them (they call `ingest_event` directly, bypassing `dispatch_event`'s gates). **(1) F-3 bootstrap chicken-and-egg:** a pushed DM `membership.join` hits the receiving node's F-3 federation-relationship gate, which requires the pusher already be in that DM's `federation_nodes` — but the join is the event that would populate it; the `drain_pending_by_federation_relationship` drain it relies on never fires for a DM (no `federation_add`). **(2) creator's pre-join message can't push:** a3 (alice's DM message, sent before bob joins) has `federation_nodes={A}` at send → nowhere to push, and the one-shot initiate catch-up streams on `shared_spaces`, never re-streaming on a later `federation_nodes` change (Option C grounded **absent** — `stream_federation_delta` is handshake-driven, single caller). **(3) replication race:** the helper can't resolve a party's home until that record replicates, and didn't re-fire on identity-replicate. All three stem from **one fact: a DM federates *late*** — it forms its content relationship at membership-apply, not at the handshake, so it lacks the relationship-formation plumbing regular Spaces get for free.

**The F1B-D8 spine came back falsified (D-065).** The Phase-0 premise that "the DM applier re-checks 2-party on the federation path" was grounded **false**: `apply_join` (state.rs:982) **open-joins** (a non-pending joiner → `Member`, J-275), and there is **no DM 2-party / join-cap gate anywhere** (the only 2-party test is invite-side). So an unconditional F-3 skip would be a **hole** (a federated peer that learns a DM's `space_id` could inject a 3rd-party open-join). F1B-D8 is therefore recorded as the **finding that drove Design Z, not a skip that shipped.**

**Design Z Joe-LOCKED + shipped (F-3 fully intact — no skip, no hole).** Populate `federation_nodes` from the DM's **parties = members ∪ pending invitees** (resolvable), not members only. For a DM `pending_invites` is exactly the one seeded counterparty (`from_dm_space_create`; further invites rejected), so the set is exactly the 2 parties **from create** → (a) the bootstrap join passes F-3 **with no skip** (joiner's home already present; a non-party's node is never in the set → F-3 still blocks 3rd parties — *no hole*, proven by the `mp_f1b_third_party_dm_join_via_federation_blocked_by_f3` unit); (b) alice's pre-join a3 pushes immediately (gap-2 closed via the **existing** push path, no backfill). Plus a new `repopulate_dm_federation_after_identity` hook fired from the existing identity-replicate handler (beside `drain_pending_by_identity`): on a record's arrival it re-populates affected DMs' `federation_nodes` and **drains any F-3-held DM join for that peer** — the replication-race fix. **D-076 discharged by inheritance:** the drain reuses `drain_pending_by_federation_relationship` **verbatim** (the same hook the `state.federation_add` trigger fires, re-dispatching via `dispatch_event` with `peer_node_id=None`) — one more trigger, no new drain, no new ordering decision. **No empty-set instant:** `apply_join`'s `pending_invites.remove` + `members.insert` are one apply, so `members ∪ pending_invites` is `{A,B}` on both sides of the pending→member transition. X (party-gated F-3 skip + bespoke backfill) rejected (looser on F-3, two new mechanisms); Option C (auto sync-on-relationship-form) rejected (the mechanism doesn't exist).

**Verification (actual).** Build 0 + clippy clean (default + `--all-features`). xgen-core **689/0** (6 units: the 4 helper-logic proofs incl. omit-unresolvable F1B-D3 + leave-shrinks, plus the Z bootstrap-passes-F3 proof + the hole-closed 3rd-party-blocked proof), xgen-node 286/0. Witness: `MP-C-07` cross-node (`mp_r1_c4`) flipped KNOWN-FAIL → **harness-green-with-boundary** — both a3 + b4 converge A↔B, **stable ×3**. **RED-on-revert genuine** (neuter the Z population → `federation_nodes` empty → bob's join F-3-held → membership diverges → RED). **No production witness claimed** (F1B-D4 — un-seeded production case not expressible on G-6 rails, sibling to MP-A-01(ii)).

**Honest boundary.** MP-C-07 converges **in the harness** because G-6 pre-seeds resolution; a production DM to a not-yet-discoverable counterparty does **not** converge until the routed **F1B-D5 "production identity→home-node discovery"** arc lands (placed on the ROADMAP horizon at this close; F1b routes to it, does not build it).

**Invariant E promoted → D-091 (D-069, at close).** Z amended its wording (members → parties): **"A DM's federation set is exactly its parties' (members ∪ pending invitees) home nodes; no other node receives DM content."** Promoted to DECISIONS as **D-091**, refining D-075 (vantage-aware derived projection) for the DM case; `DmFederationNotAllowed` stays the guard against third-party `federation_add`, F-3 stays the guard against third-party federated joins (no skip).

**Breadcrumb (folded into the close, not a standing decision).** Late-federating relationships (DMs) need explicit relationship-formation plumbing — the handshake-time stream + F-3 gate assume the relationship exists at handshake. A membership/federation arc warrants tracing what the **receiving** node does with a pushed bootstrap event, not just the sending side. Sibling to the MP-F4 design-time fold-order-probe breadcrumb; the live net caught it (third arc this loop). Surface-and-route worked again.

**Loop-to-green progress (MP-R1-D10):** MP-F2 ✅ (J-324) → MP-F3 ✅ (J-326) → MP-F1a ✅ (J-328) → MP-F4 ✅ (J-331) → **MP-F1b ✅ SHIPPED + CLOSED (J-333)** → remaining: **the 4 thin verbs** (`ban` [+MP-A-14] / `room_update` / `thread`×3 / `create-space --auth-tier`) → R1 rerun to the amended close criterion (all-green-except-MP-C-06, with MP-C-07 harness-green-with-boundary). **DECISIONS change: +D-091** (invariant E promoted). `tasks/MP_findings.md` v1.6→v1.7 (MP-F1b → Z-shipped/CLOSED); `docs/tests/MULTIPARTY_TEST_MATRIX.md` v1.6→v1.7 (MP-C-07 row); arc docs AUDIT / DESIGN (v1.1) / IMPL (v1.1) → COMPLETED. ROADMAP v3.22→v3.23. **Commit order (standing): Clair's code FIRST, then Chat's doc-bridge.** **Next-active: Clair — the 4 thin verbs** (each a small `xgen-client` production arc over an existing core builder; own per-arc discipline). **Entry point (Rule 0): CLAUDE PLAY → JOURNAL J-333 → `tasks/MP_F1B_DM_FEDERATION_DESIGN.md` §9 (Design Z) → `tasks/MP_findings.md` v1.7 (MP-F1b) → `tasks/MP_R1_DETERMINISTIC_DESIGN.md` §11 (D10).** This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

## Entry J-332 — MP-F1b Phase-0 + design v1.0 doc-bridge: gate-B FAILS production (kill-gate fired as anticipated) → Option-2 LOCKED ((iii) harness-scoped + route the discovery gap); F1B-D1..D7 Joe-LOCKED; 3 honesty conditions; MP-R1-D10 amended (MP-C-07 cross-node = harness-green-with-boundary); next-active = Clair (MP-F1b runbook)

**What happened.** Chat re-supplied (iii)/A–E/gate-B fresh to Clair (the J-327 guardrail), Clair authored + pushed the MP-F1b D-071 Phase-0 audit (commit `bfa0535`) and the design v1.0 (commit `bde00dc`) ahead of the lock (D-071, "author before runbook, lock with Joe first"). Commit order: Clair's Phase-0 + design (`bfa0535`, `bde00dc`) pushed FIRST, then this doc-bridge. This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

**Date:** 2026-06-09

**Phase-0 verdict (Clair, `bfa0535`) — GAP CONFIRMED (facet-1 real); gate-B FAILS the production case.** (iii) populates a DM Space's `federation_nodes` from the members' home nodes at membership-apply — and the home-node resolution works **in the harness** (G-6 pre-seeds the relationship + replicates identities). But there is **no production path** that resolves a not-yet-replicated counterparty's `home_node` at DM-membership-apply: `build_identity_home_nodes` (runtime.rs:1895) reads `IdentityRecord.home_node` from the local registry (registry.rs:47), and `dm_space_create` carries the *creator's* home node, not the invitee's. A fresh production DM to a stranger whose record has not replicated does not resolve. **This is the kill-gate (sub-lock B) firing exactly as J-327 anticipated — surfaced, not worked around (D-065).** There is no *small* augmentation: resolving a stranger's home node re-opens identity discovery (carry-home-in-invite presupposes discovery surfaces it; a directory is a new subsystem), which is broader than MP-F1b.

**The gate-B fork LOCKED (Joe, J-332) = Option 2 — (iii) harness-scoped + route the discovery gap.** Over Option 1 ((iii)+augment now — explodes scope into the wrong container, re-opens discovery mid-loop) and re-opening (ii)/(i) (discard correct work / breach 3.16.1 privacy). The reasoning that makes Option 2 right: **(iii) is correct *given resolved identities*; gate-B is the gap between "resolved" and "discoverable."** The DM-federation-set derivation (members' home nodes) is the right consumer of resolved identities **no matter how discovery is later solved** — the discovery arc changes *how identities enter the registry*, not *how the DM federation set is derived from known ones*. So sub-lock A is the half that stays; it is not throwaway.

**Three honesty conditions (Joe, part of the arc — F1B-D1/D4/D5):** (1) ship sub-lock A's membership-apply population; (2) record MP-C-07 cross-node honestly (a boundary, not a bare ✅); (3) the discovery gap is its own named arc.

**F1B-D1..D7 Joe-LOCKED (arc-local, D-069).** **D1** population site = a single idempotent **NodeRuntime** post-membership-apply helper (`repopulate_dm_federation_nodes`), DM-only — NOT `SpaceState` (pure, no registry), NOT `apply_federation_add` (`DmFederationNotAllowed` stays intact; no third-party node ever receives DM content); re-fires at all rebuild sites (ingest create/`derive_resolved` arm + incremental apply arm + cold-start rehydrate; the exact site list is a runbook item). **D2** the set = the **full** members' home nodes (invariant E literally), self-included for cross-node symmetry; the push path skips self (confirm at impl). **D3** the gate-B boundary lives in code **as omission** (honest-by-construction): a member whose `home_node` is not resolvable is **omitted** — no crash, no guess, no fabricated home; resolvable (harness) → federates, unresolvable (production stranger) → that node simply doesn't receive the DM, deferred behind the discovery arc. **D4** MP-C-07 (`mp_r1_c4`) recorded **with a boundary, not a bare ✅** ("DM federation forms when members' home nodes are resolvable; harness-witnessed; production convergence to a not-yet-known counterparty DEFERRED behind the identity→home discovery arc"); the un-seeded production case is **not expressible on current harness rails** (G-6 always pre-establishes federation + replication — sibling to MP-A-01(ii) PENDING), so **no production witness is claimed** (a clean green there would be the misleading-positive test-integrity forbids). **D5** the discovery gap is its own named arc — **"production identity→home-node discovery"**, the identity-resolution sibling to M9.2's still-open real-peer-discovery question; founding-philosophy territory (no-anonymity identity verification + federation discovery), genuinely bigger than F1b → **routed now as a finding, placed on the ROADMAP horizon at F1b close; F1b routes to it, does not build it.** **D6** MP-R1-D10's "all-green-except-MP-C-06" is amended to **"all-green-except-MP-C-06, with MP-C-07-cross-node harness-green-with-boundary (production convergence deferred behind the discovery arc)"** — blessed like D8/D10, mirrored into `tasks/MP_R1_DETERMINISTIC_DESIGN.md` §11. **D7** sub-locks C/D/E — C: the helper recomputes the full set at each membership-apply, so a **leave shrinks** the set naturally; the historical local copy on a departed member's node is the standing federated-RTBF tension (acknowledged, NOT solved in-arc). D: `dm_space_create` keeps riding the G-6 handshake; subsequent events use the populated set; MP-F3's `store.contains` dedup covers the overlap. E: invariant "a DM's federation set is exactly its members' home nodes; no other node receives DM content" = DECISIONS candidate, **promote per D-069 at close** once it holds across the arc.

**Composition (no reopened arcs).** The send path already consumes `federation_nodes` (`derive_event_nodes` fanout.rs:178 + `apply_federation_push` federation_session.rs:247, which already carries the origin-skip + per-peer policy filter) → the moment the set is populated, DM events federate both directions with **no** `DmFederationNotAllowed` change and **no** new send code. **MP-F4 composition (confirmed):** F1b reads **Space** membership (`state.members`), orthogonal to F4's room-scoped membership `state_key`s; F1b adds **no** `state_key`; the helper fires **after** `derive_resolved`/apply so it reads F4-correct space-membership — composes, does not reopen the shipped frontier-anchor + A1. **D-076:** `federation_nodes` is a derived projection of (resolved members × registry) — the D-075 vantage-aware shape; the full-set choice keeps it cross-node symmetric where registries agree, and where they differ (gate-B) the mptest oracle tolerates federation-infra asymmetry (MP-R1-D7); the helper reads the resolved member set → no ordering surface added. **D-077:** `DmFederationNotAllowed` intact (no privacy-containment regression); regular-Space federation untouched (DM-only); set-shrink-on-leave is new behaviour, not a regression.

**Proof plan (for the runbook).** Unit (xgen-node, NodeRuntime-level): after a DM membership-apply, `federation_nodes` = resolvable members' home nodes; an unresolvable member is **omitted** (the D3 boundary, the honest-by-construction proof); a regular Space's set is unchanged (DM-only); a leave shrinks the set. Witness: MP-C-07 cross-node (`mp_r1_c4`) flips KNOWN-FAIL → harness-green-with-boundary; **RED-on-revert** = revert the population helper → set stays empty → `apply_federation_push` early-returns → DM doesn't federate → RED (genuine, not vacuous). No production witness (recorded honestly per D4). D-076 net (`assert_converges` + 285 integration + M8) stays green; build 0 + clippy clean (default + `--features harness-control`).

Commit order: Clair's code (bc057f8) pushed FIRST, then this doc-bridge. This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

**Date:** 2026-06-09

**The mid-arc correction (D-065, the arc's standout — the MP-F3/J-326 pattern again).** The J-330 design locked A1 (room-scope the membership `state_key`) as the finding-closer. At implementation Clair built A1 (sound as keying) then **stopped and ran an empirical probe before claiming convergence** — and A1 alone failed: `space_join_id < room_join_id = false → bob in_space=true, in_room=FALSE`. Mechanism: `apply_join`'s room-level branch guards on space membership (`!members.contains_key(bob)` → `NotASpaceMember`, state.rs:988), and `fold_skipping` is single-pass in `topological_sort` order, which tie-breaks concurrent siblings **lexicographically by event_id**. A1 gives the space-join and room-join different keys (so neither is dropped by conflation) but does **not order them**; when the room-join's id sorts first it folds first, its guard fails, it no-ops → space-member-not-room, the exact finding symptom, ~50% by hash. No state-key scheme can fix an order-sensitive guard under arbitrary fold order. Surfaced not worked-around; nothing committed at the stop.

**Root cause re-grounded (sharper than the audit / J-330 design got it).** A room-join **causally depends** on its space-join (the guard enforces it), but the client emitted them **concurrent**, so the dependency was never in the DAG. Two compounding defects: **(1) missing causal edge** (client `ops::join`) — the finding's driver; **(2) room-agnostic key conflation** (node `state_key`) — the A1 target. The audit's §2.3 "trace off the critical path" call was **wrong — it was on it.** Grounding `get_dag_tips` (batch.rs) found the precise cause: it returned a **single tip (the topo-last event), not the DAG frontier** — so in MP-C-07-LOCAL, where alice's message `a3` is sent before bob joins (per the scenario `[[waits]]`), `a3` and bob's space-join `b2` are sibling leaves, and bob's room-join `b3` anchored to whichever sorts last (often `a3`) → `b3` concurrent with `b2` → the drop. MP-C-01 dodged it only because its message is gated after the room-join (no competing leaf). A general multi-leaf-frontier client bug, timing-dependent — which is why static reasoning kept saying "should work."

**Option C Joe-LOCKED + shipped (anchor-primary + A1-retained).** **The anchor is the finding-closer:** `get_dag_tips` now returns the **true DAG frontier** (all leaves not referenced as any served event's `prev_event`, sorted, capped at `MAX_PREV_EVENTS`=10) instead of the single topo-last event → a room-join causally descends from its space-join → the guard passes. Strictly-more-correct (for linear DAGs frontier == single tip → inert); a general client-anchoring correctness fix that happens to close MP-F4, affecting all `get_dag_tips` callers (`join`/`leave`/`send`/…). **A1 retained** as the latent-conflation defense (scope-aware membership `state_key` across join/leave/kick — the J-330 widening; invite/ban/eject/unban stay space-level) — sound, cheap, guards genuine concurrent-membership conflations (two-device, federation-reorder) the anchor doesn't touch (D-077-forward). B (a fold-order rule in `derive_resolved`) rejected (D-076-sensitive, wrong layer — works around a missing causal edge instead of encoding it); A (anchor-only) rejected (discards sound A1).

**Verification (actual).** Build 0 + clippy clean (default `--all-features` + `--features harness-control`). xgen-core 683/0 (A1 keying units + 4 convergence witnesses), xgen-node 286/0, xgen-client 103/0 + integration green. Heavy: `MP-C-07-LOCAL` flipped delivery-only → **2-party DM message convergence** (a3 + b4 land on Node A) PASS; MP-C-01 contrast PASS (now concurrency-robust). **All-callers / D-076 / D-077 sweep discharged green** — no single-tip-dependent test broke; multi-parent `prev_events` already legal; no wire / persistence / reason-string change. **Sensitivity (honest, D-065):** the clean RED-on-revert is the **unit probe** (A1-alone → room-join dropped, deterministic); the heavy MP-C-07-LOCAL revert is **fold-order-flaky** (the bug is ~50% by hash), recorded as such rather than dressed up as a uniform RED.

**Honest boundary.** MP-F4 closes **single-node** 2-party DM convergence. The **federated** MP-C-07 (cross-node) stays KNOWN-FAIL → MP-F1b (facet-1, (iii) membership-driven DM federation).

**Breadcrumb (folded into the corrected design, not a standing decision).** Membership/resolution arcs warrant an **empirical fold-order probe at design time**, not just impl — this is the second arc where the live net caught a fold/order subtlety reasoning missed (MP-F3 gate-placement, now MP-F4 fold-order). The surface-and-route discipline worked exactly as intended both times.

**Loop-to-green progress (MP-R1-D10):** MP-F2 ✅ (J-324) → MP-F3 ✅ (J-326) → MP-F1a ✅ (J-328) → **MP-F4 ✅ SHIPPED + CLOSED (J-331)** → remaining: **MP-F1b** (facet-1, (iii)) + 4 thin verbs → R1 rerun. No DECISIONS change (F4-D# / Option C arc-local, D-069). `tasks/MP_findings.md` v1.4→v1.5 (MP-F4 RESOLVED); matrix v1.5→v1.6 (MP-C-07 row updated); arc docs AUDIT / DESIGN (v1.2) / IMPL (v1.1) → COMPLETED. ## Entry J-330 — MP-F4 design Joe-LOCKED (F4-D1..D5; A1 confirmed + the join/leave/kick room-scope widening locked); spine proof = guard+cascade complementarity (ban-evasion closed); design 861b4ab; next-active = Clair (MP-F4 runbook)

**What happened.** Clair authored + committed the MP-F4 design (commit 861b4ab, `tasks/MP_F4_DM_MEMBERSHIP_DESIGN.md`) on the locked F4-A=A1, with the cross-scope-conflict proof as its spine, and surfaced one scope sharpening for Joe. Joe confirmed the widening and locked the design. Chat doc-only follow (this entry): records the design-lock + the A1-scope sharpening + the three-pair D-076 witness obligation; this PLAY/JOURNAL/ROADMAP. Commit order: Clair's design (861b4ab) pushed FIRST, then this doc-bridge. This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.

**Date:** 2026-06-09

**Design Joe-LOCKED (F4-D1..D5, arc-local, D-069).** **F4-D1** the key transform: `state_key_for_event`'s membership key stays `membership:{space}:{id}` when `room_id` is empty (space-level), becomes `membership:{space}:room:{room}:{id}` when populated (room-level) — one edit site (state_key.rs) + one helper. **F4-D2** the spine (below). **F4-D3:** all 5 production readers consume `StateKey` opaquely; `StateKey` is never serialized → no migration, no wire / reason-string change; appliers untouched. **F4-D4** witness: MP-C-07-LOCAL delivery-only → 2-party message convergence (a3 + b4), genuinely RED on revert (also confirms alice's a3 lands post-MP-F1a). **F4-D5:** F1b cross-link flagged not merged; federated MP-C-07 stays KNOWN-FAIL.

**The spine (F4-D2) — cross-scope-conflict proof, proven not assumed.** Once room-level and space-level membership occupy different key-groups, a space-level removal (ban/kick/leave) still dominates a room-level join across ALL orderings, via guard + cascade being complementary: (i) removal folds before room-join → `apply_join`'s room-level guard (`!members.contains_key(id)` → `NotASpaceMember`) makes the join a no-op → id ∉ members, ∉ room; (ii) room-join folds before removal → the removal's cascade (`for room … room.members.remove(id)`) undoes the join's insert → id ∉ members, ∉ room. Both orderings converge identically with no shared key. §5.6 pins the concurrent-ban-vs-room-join permutations to "banned, in no room" under every order → **A1 opens no ban-evasion.**

**A1-scope sharpening Joe-LOCKED (Clair-surfaced, D-065).** J-329 locked A1 as "room-scope join/leave; space-level ops stay room-agnostic." Grounding the appliers showed **kick and leave also have room-level branches, and room-level leave is live** (`ops::leave --room`; `KickArgs.room` wired). Today room-level join/leave/kick all share the room-agnostic key, so a room-kick and a room-join of the same id in the same room conflict and converge *by sharing it*. Room-scoping only `join` would leave room-kick on the old key and room-join on the new one → they stop conflicting → a NEW room-kick-vs-room-join non-convergence. So **A1 is scope-aware across all three room-capable events (join/leave/kick)** — a correctness requirement, not scope-creep; invite/ban/eject/unban stay always-space-level (no room branch). This completes the audit's "join/leave" framing rather than contradicting it; the principle (room-level membership events get a room dimension, space-level ones do not) is intact.

**D-076 re-proven set = THREE pairs (the widening enlarges the convergence surface).** Each must be genuinely RED on revert: (1) cross-scope removal × room-join (F4-D2); (2) room-kick × room-join (same room-scoped key, conflict preserved); (3) room-leave × room-join (same room-scoped key, conflict preserved). The runbook's witness set must test all three — the widening's correctness is tested, not asserted. Space-level keys stay byte-identical (existing conflicts untouched); only the wrongly-conflated facts separate. D-077: MP-C-01 stays green and becomes robust (was luck-dependent).

**Open colour, off the critical path (audit §2.3).** The proximate-cause ambiguity (a staleness window vs the `get_dag_tips` fallback as the concurrency source) is not resolved — A1 fixes the domain regardless; a runtime trace is optional, not gating.

**Loop-to-green progress (MP-R1-D10):** MP-F2 ✅ (J-324) → MP-F3 ✅ (J-326) → MP-F1a ✅ (J-328) → MP-F4 Phase-0 + A1-lock (J-329) → **MP-F4 design Joe-LOCKED (J-330)** → remaining: MP-F4 runbook→impl→close, then MP-F1b (facet-1, iii) + 4 thin verbs → R1 rerun. No DECISIONS change (F4-D# arc-local, D-069). `tasks/MP_F4_DM_MEMBERSHIP_DESIGN.md` (861b4ab) → v1.1 to lock the join/leave/kick widening language (Clair, riding the runbook commit). ROADMAP v3.19→v3.20. **Commit order (standing): Clair's code/arc-doc FIRST, then Chat's doc-bridge.** **Next-active: Clair — author `tasks/MP_F4_DM_MEMBERSHIP_IMPL.md`** (runbook; the three-pair D-076 witness set is a hard deliverable) → implement → close. **Entry point (Rule 0): CLAUDE PLAY → JOURNAL J-330 → `tasks/MP_F4_DM_MEMBERSHIP_DESIGN.md` (F4-D1..D5 + §5.6 spine) → `tasks/MP_F4_DM_MEMBERSHIP_AUDIT.md` v1.1 → `tasks/MP_R1_DETERMINISTIC_DESIGN.md` §11 (D10).** This doc set not pushed — Joe pushes.
